title: Generating Long Semantic IDs in Parallel for Recommendation

problem.claim: Generative semantic ID-based recommendation models have inefficient inference because they rely on resource-intensive beam search and multiple forward passes.

gap.claim: Short semantic IDs, typically restricted to about 4 tokens, limit expressiveness.

contributions.claim: RPG is a lightweight framework for semantic ID-based recommendation that produces unordered, long semantic IDs so tokens can be predicted in parallel.
RPG independently predicts each token with a multi-token prediction loss and uses a similarity graph during inference to avoid invalid IDs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that using semantic IDs of length 64 improves NDCG@10 by an average of 12.6% over generative baselines and improves inference efficiency.
The authors report that code is available in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Semantic IDs represent items with a small number of discrete tokens intended to preserve semantics while improving recommendation performance, scalability, and memory efficiency.
Generative approaches incur inefficient inference, which restricts semantic ID length and limits expressiveness.
RPG addresses these challenges with unordered, long semantic IDs, independent token prediction, a multi-token prediction loss, and graph-guided decoding.
The authors report that length-64 semantic IDs outperform generative baselines by an average of 12.6% on NDCG@10 while improving inference efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that independent parallel token prediction enables semantic IDs of length 64 and improves reported recommendation performance and inference efficiency.

interpretation.claim: Parallelizing prediction can reduce the inference cost that constrains the expressiveness of autoregressive representations.

application.claim: When sequential decoding limits representation length, consider unordered factorization with an objective that preserves token-level semantics and decoding constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond the reported recommendation setting or how much performance depends on the graph-guided decoding mechanism.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, experimental protocol, and statistical uncertainty are not specified.
The relative contributions of the parallel prediction loss and graph-guided decoding are not isolated.
Details of the invalid-ID constraint, model architecture, and computational efficiency measurements are omitted.
